hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $0$.
And the point at $0$ is filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything **less than or equal to $0$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**


[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 0 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at 0 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < 0$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 0 and continues left. An open point is plotted at 0 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3ba1eb5c568b51cf72b7640503adab75c7e20818)

The graph of $x > 0$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 0 and continues right. An open point is plotted at 0 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/425c273291a50896db90fef4495d9a36bec3d02d)

The graph of $x \geq 0$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 0 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at 0 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/f62de34c65221fb73bfd3e3a2d657803de7978c3)
